chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who divorced his wife, or she performed khula' (redemption), or barr' (mutual release), is it permissible for him to marry her sister? He said: 'When her bond of marriage is dissolved and he has no right of return to her, then he may propose marriage to her sister.'

key_terms.اخْتَلَعَتْ: She performed khula' (divorce initiated by wife with compensation)
key_terms.عِصْمَتُهَا: Her bond of marriage / her sanctity

ai.seo_question: When can a man marry his ex-wife's sister after divorce?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific condition for the permissibility of marrying two sisters: the prohibition is contingent upon the first wife's 'ismah' (marital bond) still being active with the right of return (raj'ah). Once the divorce becomes irrevocable and the waiting period concludes, the restriction lifts, allowing the man to marry the sister. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between temporary and permanent prohibitions of kinship marriage.
